extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: A bilingual, multitask benchmark for long context understanding comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in English and Chinese, standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of LLMs.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench was constructed from 21 datasets using three approaches: direct extraction from original datasets, building from original datasets with processing for long-context evaluation, and newly created and annotated datasets by the authors. Public datasets were mainly extracted from test sets to avoid leakage, with random sampling used for LongBench and uniform sampling by length used for LongBench-E.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include original public datasets and collected documents/articles from literature, film, science papers, legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers, Wikipedia, Baidu Search, Baidu Zhidao, meetings, news, web questions, dialogue, C4 Chinese sections, GitHub code, and GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Datasets were adapted for long-context evaluation by selecting long documents or segments, adding supporting and distracting passages up to a maximum length, randomly ordering passages, concatenating documents with markers, constructing few-shot contexts from sampled training examples, generating synthetic tasks through random sampling/repetition/shuffling, and shuffling cross-file code snippets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The benchmark standardized all datasets into a unified format. Additional preprocessing included filtering TriviaQA passages with fewer than 1,000 words, selecting long segments from VCSUM, extracting from public test sets to avoid leakage, and sampling by length ranges for LongBench-E.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Five datasets were created and annotated by the authors. For MultiFieldQA in English and Chinese, the authors manually curated documents from multiple sources and invited three Ph.D. students to annotate question-answer pairs for each article, aiming for definitive answers suitable for automated evaluation and ensuring answers were inferable from documents with evidence placement kept fairly random. Some source datasets also contained human-written summaries or annotator-created questions/paraphrases.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process aimed to reduce bias by ensuring answers were inferable from documents and that evidence placement was fairly random rather than concentrated at the beginning or end.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students; NLP practitioners for Qasper source annotations; native speakers for HotpotQA source questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential bias from answer evidence appearing disproportionately at the beginning or end of documents was considered during annotation. The benchmark also discusses memorization bias because some tasks are derived from Wikipedia, a common LLM pretraining source, and evaluation bias from automatic metrics and LLM-as-examiner.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include potentially unreliable automatic metrics such as ROUGE-L and F1, which may underestimate models that generate longer responses; high runtime overhead and bias when using LLMs as evaluators; and coupling of benchmark performance with instruction-following capabilities rather than isolating long-context modeling alone.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended for evaluating and benchmarking LLM long-context understanding, including zero-shot evaluation across six task categories and analysis of model capability across varying context lengths via LongBench-E.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce LongBench, the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding

description.evidence: LongBench comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese). These tasks cover key long-text application areas including single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. All datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format, allowing for effortless automatic evaluation of LLMs.

inLanguage.evidence: LongBench comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese

rai:dataCollection.evidence: All 21 datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format, among which 6 are directly extracted from the original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 are built based on the original datasets and processed to be suitable for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by us. Since LLMs may have already been trained on the training set of some of our collected public datasets, to avoid test leakage, we extract data from the test sets of these public datasets, with the exception of VCSUM due to its insufficient data in its test set. We employ two extraction strategies: random sampling and uniform sampling.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: 6 are directly extracted from the original datasets provided by previous studies, 10 are built based on the original datasets and processed to be suitable for long context evaluation, and 5 are created and annotated by us. We first collect documents and articles from multiple sources, including legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers, etc.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We first collect documents and articles from multiple sources, including legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers, etc (sources detailed in Appendix). Table 1: 'Source' denotes the origin of the context. ... NarrativeQA Literature, Film ... Qasper Science ... HotpotQA Wikipedia ... DuReader Baidu Search ... GovReport Government report ... VCSUM Meeting ... TREC Web question ... PassageRetrieval-zh C4 Dataset ... LCC Github ... RepoBench-P Github repository

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: To tailor the data for long-context evaluation, we utilize complete Wikipedia passages encompassing the supporting or distracting paragraphs as the context. Initially, supporting passages are included within the context, and then as many distracting passages are added until the total length reaches a maximum length. Finally, these passages are randomly ordered to form the multi-document context. In LongBench, we include “Document i” before the ith news article, and concatenate them into the context C. In each of the above datasets adapted for LongBench, for each test data, we first randomly select an integer within a range as the number of examples, then randomly sample the corresponding number of samples from the training set, and concatenate them to form the context C. For each piece of data, we randomly select several passages from English Wikipedia, repeat each paragraph at random several times, and finally shuffle the paragraphs. For each original piece of data, we shuffle the cross-file code snippets that include the gold cross-file code snippet ... and combine them into context C.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: All datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format, allowing for effortless automatic evaluation of LLMs. We filter the passages in TriviaQA with less than 1,000 words to be examples. In LongBench, we select the long segments from VCSUM to compose our evaluation samples. Since LLMs may have already been trained on the training set of some of our collected public datasets, to avoid test leakage, we extract data from the test sets of these public datasets... During the uniform sampling process, we use word count as the length and sample a comparable quantity of data from the length ranges of 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: 5 are created and annotated by us. To better test the model’s long context understanding ability across diverse fields, we manually curate the MultiFieldQA datasets in both English and Chinese. We invite three Ph.D. students to annotate the question and answer for each article, with definitive answers as much as possible for ease of automated evaluation. During the annotation, we ensure that the answers can be inferred from the documents, and the placement of evidence is fairly random to avoid biases

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: During the annotation, we ensure that the answers can be inferred from the documents, and the placement of evidence is fairly random to avoid biases that might occur if, for instance, the answer-related statements are frequently found at the beginning or the end

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We invite three Ph.D. students to annotate the question and answer for each article. We also sample from Qasper (Dasigi et al., 2021), which features QA over NLP papers and is annotated by NLP practitioners. rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: For each data entry, we randomly sample 30 passages and select one of them for summarization using GPT-3.5-Turbo.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: During the annotation, we ensure that the answers can be inferred from the documents, and the placement of evidence is fairly random to avoid biases that might occur if, for instance, the answer-related statements are frequently found at the beginning or the end... We observe that the memorization performance (w/o context) on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MusiQue is relatively high. This is likely because these datasets are derived from Wikipedia, a common source for training prevalent LLMs. ... LLM also has bias when used as an evaluation metric

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Despite LongBench offers a more comprehensive testbed for long context understanding, it still has its shortcomings... (1) Potentially unreliable automatic metrics: As previous studies suggest (Bai et al., 2023), the automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect the quality of the response. Particularly, the results on these metrics may be underestimated for models that are used to generating longer responses... LLM also has bias when used as an evaluation metric... (2) Coupling with instruction-following capabilities... Consequently, the performance on LongBench is coupled with the models’ instruction-following capabilities.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce LongBench, the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, enabling a more rigorous evaluation of long context understanding. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 8 models on LongBench... Additionally, to better disentangle the models’ long context ability from their task ability, we construct LongBench-E that features a more even length distribution, thus suited for gauging each model’s capability across various context lengths. We conduct the assessment in a zero-shot setting, except for the few-shot learning tasks where the few-shot examples are provided as part of the long context.
